forecast-period.text: A high pressure system centred well south of SA will continue to drift eastwards over the weekend, while a developing low pressure system and trough in WA move close to the SA border. The high drifts southeast of Tasmania by Monday as the low moves across western SA on Monday and northern SA on Tuesday before clearing to the east later. Another high develops south of the bight on Wednesday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Frost patches about the southeast. Possible showers or thunderstorms in the west, more likely west of Ceduna during the afternoon, possibly extending into central districts during the late afternoon or evening. Maximum temperatures below average, grading to above average in the west. Moderate to fresh southeast to northeasterly winds, shifting southwest to southeasterly in the far west later.

Possible showers or thunderstorms in the west, more likely in the far northwest during the afternoon, with gusty winds possible. Moderate to fresh south to southeasterly winds, shifting east to northeasterly in the west.

Possible showers or thunderstorms about the pastoral districts and adjacent parts of the agricultural area. Maximum temperatures generally above average. East to northeasterly winds, freshening about western and central parts, ahead of a fresh southwest to southerly change moving across western parts during the day.

Possible showers or thunderstorms about the pastoral districts, adjacent parts of the agricultural area and in the east. Maximum temperatures above average in the east and far north, grading to below average in the west. Moderate to fresh northeast to northwesterly winds about eastern parts at first, with fresh southwest to southeasterly winds in the west. extending throughout during the day.

text.p: Possible showers or thunderstorms about the far north and west. Maximum temperatures above average in the northeast, grading to below average elsewhere. Southwest to southeasterly winds.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Wednesday: Broadly less than 2 mm across the state. Falls increasing to 2 to 5 mm about the northwest and far north, with isolated falls of 5 to 15 mm possible about the west and parts of the northern agricultural area and 10 to 20 mm with thunderstorms.
